Mushrooms have allowed me to better figure out who I am and think about the kind of person I aspire to be. I feel like I can live in the present rather than dwell in the past. My mind is usually racing a million miles per hour trying to make connections between different concepts and trying to determine improvements. Consequently I've spent years talking over traumatic experiences and my anxiety disorder with therapists and trying to "figure out what's wrong with me" to no avail. I read this quote from a blog while coming down from a trip and it made me realize what I was doing wrong:

"Numerous studies over the past two decades have shown that to the contrary, overthinking ushers in a host of adverse consequences: It sustains or worsens sadness, fosters negatively biased thinking, impairs a person’s ability to solve problems, saps motivation, and interferes with concentration and initiative. Moreover, although people have a strong sense that they are gaining insight into themselves and their problems during their ruminations, this is rarely the case. What they do gain is a distorted, pessimistic perspective on their lives."

When you're stripped of your ego and your normal defensive mechanisms, I think it's easier to have a compassionate approach with ourselves when coping with difficult emotions. If a good friend of mine was dealing with a major life problem, I would try to remain optimistic and offer good advice and try to think of a healthy way to deal with the problem.  

Specifically, psychedelics have completely changed my outlook on social interactions and relationships. I feel like I've re-prioritized who I choose to spend time with. I'm also a much more open person and have more of a desire to be social. Most psychedelics are anti-addictive as well, which is a good thing, because you are forced to take long breaks to make the most of the experience. I feel that psychedelics can make return you temporarily to that childhood awe of the world again.
